quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by closing the throttle gradually. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to help others see you.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: How can you help drivers merging onto the highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Move to the next lane if you can.
Do nothing. They need to merge safely on their own.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the next lane if you can.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by changing lanes if possible.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes a vehicle on a two-lane road, how should they pass?

options.text: In a staggered formation with several riders passing at once.

questions.explanation: When a group passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider should pass one at a time. One rider must finish passing before the next rider begins.

questions.question: What percentage of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: In a normal turn, how should the motorcycle and rider lean?

options.text: The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays upright.
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays upright.

questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen best?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to make yourself visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you on your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, downshift and approach the dog slowly. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not try to kick the dog.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader. This puts them near the front where more experienced riders at the back can watch them.

questions.question: When slowing down or stopping, what should you do with the gears?

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Keep the bike in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What usually causes a motorcycle to move into another lane while turning?
questions.explanation: Entering a turn at too high a speed can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: What can cause the front wheel and handlebars to shake or wobble?

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the other driver will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee the other driver will yield to you.
It means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the other driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: What should a passenger never do on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 in South Carolina must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that could catch on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator when turning. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated with your left foot. Lift your foot under the lever to shift up. Push down to shift down.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a lead rider extends their left arm straight out with palm down and swings it down to their side, riders should slow down.

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to have a conflict with other traffic?
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict happens at intersections where other vehicles may cross your path. Stay alert at intersections.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs a longer distance to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black text. They tell drivers about road rules. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders ride?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they lead.
They may slow the group down as leaders.
They will ride too fast in other positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them closely.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, denim pants, and full-fingered gloves protect you in a fall. Wear lace-up boots or high-top boots instead of athletic shoes. These boots protect your ankles.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to be more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be visible, wear bright clothing with reflective material, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: What should you do to react faster in an emergency?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes
Pull in the clutch when turning

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping centers, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to danger.
